newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps drift sideways but mogas stronger.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps drift sideways but mogas stronger.

text.p: European oil swaps trudged sideways on Thursday with values little changed except for gasoline which was $2 stronger.
"It's the classic summer time blues," said one trader of the poor activity.
Dealers said flat screen crude and the absence of any change in the market fundamentals had led to a quiet day.

Prompt gasoline swaps built on Wednesday's U.S.-led gains, but further out swaps were unchanged, extending the $4.50 backwardation to $7 or so. August was pegged around $195.75 from $193.75 while September was unchanged at $188.50-$190 with October only marginally firmer by 50 cents or so at $185.
Brent CFDs were broadly unchanged throughout the day with only one roll heard done. August 11-15 against August 18-22 traded at +3 cents.
Values for July 28-August 1 CFDs were put steady at +9 cents against September Brent with August 4-8 hovering around -6 cents compared with -5 cents.
August 11-15 was put at -11 cents from -12 cents and August 18-22 was talked, but not traded at -14/15 cents.

Heavy fuel swaps drifted sideways with August shuffling around $90 and September about $1 in contango. Physical barges were sold at $90.25 fob Rotterdam and $91 fob Antwerp. A Med swap traded at $82.75 for August.

Naphtha swaps saw August broadly steady to 25 cents firmer on August around $186 with September continuing to be backwardated by $1 while October was flat. August traded at $186 and $186.50 and September was done at $184.75.
